'''Jon Kjell Gjønnes''' (26 January 1931 – 6 April 2021) was a Norwegian physicist.

==Career==
Born in [[Brevik, Norway|Brevik]], Gjønnes graduated as [[cand. real.]] from the [[University of Oslo]] in 1957, and as [[dr.philos.]] in 1967. He was appointed professor at the [[University of Oslo]] in 1982. His research contributions were mainly in the fields of [[x-ray diffraction]], [[electron diffraction]] and [[electron microscopy]].<ref name=snl>{{cite encyclopedia|title=Jon Gjønnes |first=Bjørn |last=Pedersen |authorlink=Bjørn Pedersen |encyclopedia=[[Store norske leksikon]] |editor-last=Bolstad | editor-first=Erik |publisher=Norsk nettleksikon |location=Oslo |url=https://snl.no/Jon_Gjønnes |language=no |access-date=29 April 2021}}</ref> 

In 2008 he was the inaugural recipient of a medal for outstanding contribution to the Field of Electron crystallography, from the [[International Union of Crystallography]]; the medal was named the ''Gjønnes Medal'' in his honour.<ref name=snl/> He was a fellow of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]] from 1987.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=26857|title=Utenlandske medlemmer|publisher=[[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]]|language=no|access-date=2 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070715142138/http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=26857|archive-date=15 July 2007}}</ref>

Gjønnes was also an elected member of [[Bærum]] [[municipal council (Norway)|municipal council]] and from 1979 to 1981 a political adviser in [[Nordli's Cabinet]].<ref name=snl/>
